header.objective: Integrate real FUERZAS + LISTA kernels into phase5_main_fixed.cu

integration_summary.step_6_monitor_gpu: ✓ PARTIAL - SM%=0 due to workload size (not a code issue)

fuerzas_lj.purpose: Lennard-Jones force calculation with atomic ops

status.root_cause: N=99 too small; O(N²) kernels complete in microseconds; SM utilization requires sustained multi-millisecond compute

notes: Phase5 kernels (LISTA and FUERZAS) are REAL GPU code, not stubs
LISTA: computes full N×N distance matrix via grid-stride kernel
FUERZAS: computes LJ forces with atomic force accumulation per atom
SM%=0 is NOT a code structure issue; it's a workload size issue
For N=99 atoms, total GPU work is O(N²)=9801 pairs per step
Total time: 93ms / 10000 steps = 9.3µs/step; kernel overhead dominates actual compute
To achieve SM%>50%: need N >= 1024 atoms (1M+ pairs per step) or longer kernel runtime

validation.reason: Energy values are NOT being transferred back from GPU to host; cudaMemcpy returns before energy reduction kernels complete

sm_utilization.solution: Increase N to >= 1024 atoms; O(N²) workload will consume > 10ms per step
sm_utilization.rationale: 1024² = 1,048,576 pairs; FUERZAS kernel will run for ~10-50ms

energy_collection.target: Correct energy values with >=6 decimal precision
energy_collection.fix: Add cudaMemcpy(h_ke_sum, d_ke_sum, ...) after kernel + explicit stream sync before copy

next_steps: 1. Scale to N>=1024 for meaningful SM% measurement
2. Fix energy retrieval: async memcpy needs explicit sync
3. Validate physics vs Fortran with corrected energy values
4. Profile with nsys for detailed kernel timing breakdown
